question: What does Taiwan stock-level day-trading activity measure, and can it be used as a directional chip signal?
officialSemantics: TWSE defines same-day trading as opposite buy/sell transactions in the same account and security during the same business day under eligible rules.
TWSE publishes stock-level day-trading shares and buy/sell values plus market-level day-trading shares.
TPEx also exposes day-trading market and stock-level statistics.
TWSE official data product is produced after market close; historical report pages exist.
positiveMechanisms: High day-trading share may proxy attention, short-horizon speculation, liquidity demand and faster inventory turnover.
When combined with weak price acceptance, leverage/crowding and high volatility it may describe fragile speculative crowding.
When combined with strong depth/liquidity and persistent price acceptance it may instead reflect healthy liquidity/participation.
falsification: High day-trading activity can increase liquidity and price discovery rather than instability.
A high absolute day-trading share count mainly proxies liquid/high-turnover stocks unless normalized.
Buy and sell notional are close by construction for completed round trips and do not identify overnight directional inventory.
Eligibility rules, disposition/altered-trading status and rule changes create regime discontinuities.
Market-wide high day-trading regimes can make a stock-level raw threshold meaningless; use cross-sectional/own-history context.
exactNext: Capture prospective same-day availability before the after-market decision clock, then test day-trading share as context conditional on price-volume, volatility, leverage and regime. No standalone day-trading score.
